target: is_late (1 = delivered after the estimated delivery calendar date)

dropped_candidates.customer_city: high cardinality (3,694 distinct values in 64,053 training orders, median 2 orders each); state captures the coarse geography
dropped_candidates.seller_city: high cardinality (470 distinct values in 64,053 training orders, median 8 orders each); state captures the coarse geography
dropped_candidates.state_pair: high-cardinality interaction of seller_state x customer_state; the two states plus same_state already carry it
dropped_candidates.n_products: secondary order-size aggregate overlapping n_items (Spearman rho = 0.55 on the training window); kept for analytics only to limit redundancy
dropped_candidates.n_categories: secondary order-size aggregate overlapping n_items (Spearman rho = 0.13 on the training window); kept for analytics only to limit redundancy
dropped_candidates.weight_missing: covered by the median imputer's missing-value indicator on the weight / dimension columns
dropped_candidates.purchase_date: excluded by design: raw date is a time-drift proxy; calendar effects enter only through day-of-week
dropped_candidates.purchase_year: excluded by design: a year column only identifies the period (time-drift proxy) and can never generalise to unseen years
dropped_candidates.purchase_year_month: excluded by design: a month identifier is a time-drift proxy
dropped_candidates.purchase_quarter: redundant with purchase_month (Spearman rho = 0.96 on the training window)
dropped_candidates.purchase_month: calendar month cannot be separated from one-off events when training covers little more than one year; removing it did not lower the MEAN validation PR-AUC across Logistic regression and Histogram gradient boosting (with -> without: Logistic regression 0.139 -> 0.135 (-0.003, lowered); Histogram gradient boosting 0.108 -> 0.135 (+0.027, raised); mean change +0.012). It lowered Logistic regression individually, so the drop is driven by the other model(s). The rule is applied on the validation window, which is also used for tuning and model choice.

features.rare_category_handling: one-hot with min_frequency=50: rarer levels are grouped

split.method: chronological by order_purchase_timestamp: train earliest, validation middle, test latest (start inclusive, end exclusive; orders are the unit so no order is in two partitions)
notes: 267 orders purchased before 2017-01-01 (2016-09 to 2016-12) are excluded: the marketplace had almost no volume yet (at most 265 orders in any month), too sparse to learn from or evaluate on.

Late rate by window: train 7.98% (n=64,053), validation 4.17% (n=19,643), test 4.81% (n=12,507). The spread between the highest and lowest window is 3.8 percentage points, so thresholds and probabilities fitted on one regime are applied to another and test precision / calibration can differ from validation partly because of the base-rate shift.

Non-stationarity: Late rate by month inside the training window: highest 2018-03 (19.0%), 2018-02 (14.1%), 2017-11 (12.4%) versus a median of 4.4%. The top month is 4.3x the median: episodes of elevated delay like this may not be anticipated from purchase-time order attributes alone, which would limit any purchase-time model.

Covariate / concept drift (descriptive, computed per window): train: median promise 24 days, late rate same-state 4.6% vs other-state 9.7%; validation: median promise 25 days, late rate same-state 2.3% vs other-state 5.4%; test: median promise 17 days, late rate same-state 7.4% vs other-state 3.0%. The same-state minus other-state late-rate gap changes sign between windows (train -5.1 pp, validation -3.1 pp, test +4.4 pp): an association learned on the earlier window may not transfer to the later one.
Month-of-year / quarter are tested as features (see features.dropped_candidates): the modelled history spans 1.7 years, so a month effect cannot be separated from one-off events in a single year.

Selection bias / right-censoring: labels exist only for delivered orders. In the test window 145 of 12,824 orders (1.13%) are still in an open status (created/approved/invoiced/processing/shipped) at the end of the data and cannot be labelled; if those orders are disproportionately late, the late rate of the latest months is understated (by at most the share of open orders). Latest recorded delivery: 2018-10-17. Cancelled / unavailable orders are also unlabelled.

The final model is fitted on the training window only (not refitted on train+validation) so that validation-based calibration, thresholds and bands remain honest; this ignores the most recent weeks before the test window.

Out-of-support orders (a numeric feature outside the training-window min-max range, where the model can only extrapolate): validation: 0.02% of 19,643 orders (mostly total_price, 0.01%); late rate 0.0% (n=3) vs 4.2% for the rest; test: 10.10% of 12,507 orders (mostly estimated_delivery_days, 10.07%); late rate 16.9% (n=1,263) vs 3.5% for the rest.

selected_model.name: logistic_regression
selected_model.rationale: Primary metric: validation PR-AUC (average precision), because only 4.2% of validation orders are late. Best uncalibrated score: Logistic regression (0.138); models within one paired-bootstrap standard deviation of it: Logistic regression, Histogram gradient boosting. Logistic regression was chosen as the simplest of those (uncalibrated validation PR-AUC 0.138, 95% bootstrap interval 0.125-0.158) versus the 0.042 no-skill baseline (= validation late rate), i.e. a 3.3x lift. isotonic calibration kept (fitted on validation). Mean predicted risk vs observed late rate: validation 4.2% vs 4.2%; test 7.5% vs 4.8%. Test window (untouched until the end; n=12,507, 4.8% late): ROC-AUC 0.617 (validation 0.781); PR-AUC 0.073 vs no-skill 0.048 = 1.5x lift (validation 3.4x on the same scores), 95% bootstrap interval 0.064-0.083 (1.3x-1.7x); Brier 0.0487 vs 0.0468 for the constant baseline; log-loss 0.2019 vs 0.2006; mean predicted risk 7.5% vs observed 4.8%. WARNING: On the test window the model's Brier score is not better than the constant baseline, so its probabilities are not better calibrated than simply quoting the base rate. On the test window the model's log-loss is not better than the constant baseline. Test lift (interval 1.3x-1.7x) is clearly below validation lift (3.4x): performance degraded on the later window; expect weaker results in use than the validation figures suggest. Calibration lowered test PR-AUC (0.079 uncalibrated -> 0.073).

risk_bands.definition: Bands are probability cuts taken from the VALIDATION scores of the selected model: High = approximately the top 5% of validation orders (probability >= 0.165); Moderate = approximately the next 15% (probability >= 0.064); Low = the rest. Tied scores cannot be split, so the actual validation shares are High 5.3%, Moderate 15.4%, Low 79.3%. Observed late rates per band are shown for validation (in-sample for the cuts) and test (out-of-sample). Validation: Observed late rate rises monotonically from Low to High. Adjacent bands have non-overlapping 95% Wilson intervals. Test: Observed late rate rises monotonically from Low to High. The 95% Wilson intervals of adjacent bands overlap for Moderate-High: those bands cannot be told apart at this sample size. Bands are associations, not guarantees. Test-window late rate by band, same-state vs other-state orders (descriptive): Low 4.7% (n=3,964) vs 1.0% (n=2,926); Moderate 16.0% (n=1,118) vs 2.5% (n=2,638); High 20.5% (n=83) vs 6.9% (n=1,778). Mean predicted vs observed risk: same-state 4.3% vs 7.4% (n=5,165), other-state 9.8% vs 3.0% (n=7,342); the pooled band rates above average over these two groups.

metric_guidance: Only 4.8% of test orders are late, so accuracy is misleading: predicting 'on time' for every order scores 95.2% accuracy with zero late orders found. Prefer PR-AUC (average precision; the no-skill baseline equals the late rate), recall at a useful precision (see the risk bands and precision / recall in the top 10% of scores), ROC-AUC (ranking quality, 0.5 = no skill) and calibration (Brier score and the calibration curve: do predicted probabilities match observed rates?). Performance degraded on the later test window (delay regimes shift over time): Test window (untouched until the end; n=12,507, 4.8% late): ROC-AUC 0.617 (validation 0.781); PR-AUC 0.073 vs no-skill 0.048 = 1.5x lift (validation 3.4x on the same scores), 95% bootstrap interval 0.064-0.083 (1.3x-1.7x); Brier 0.0487 vs 0.0468 for the constant baseline; log-loss 0.2019 vs 0.2006; mean predicted risk 7.5% vs observed 4.8%. WARNING: On the test window the model's Brier score is not better than the constant baseline, so its probabilities are not better calibrated than simply quoting the base rate. On the test window the model's log-loss is not better than the constant baseline. Test lift (interval 1.3x-1.7x) is clearly below validation lift (3.4x): performance degraded on the later window; expect weaker results in use than the validation figures suggest. Calibration lowered test PR-AUC (0.079 uncalibrated -> 0.073).
